payload.title: Keep videos rated two stars or lower out of public indexes
payload.description:
As a Machines on Machines editor, I can rate a video two stars or lower to keep it out of every public video index while preserving direct editorial links from related articles and posts.

Observed regression: videos BRquAFLHgfE and y_BUOhAXUWM are rated 2. After rerender, the homepage omits them but /videos/ still lists them.

Acceptance

Scenario: a rating of two or lower excludes a video from every public video index
  Given an accepted video is rated two stars or lower
  When the public site is rebuilt
  Then the video is absent from the homepage Worth Watching list, /videos/, every page of its pagination, and any section-specific /<section>/videos/ listing
  And its accepted state is unchanged

Scenario: a rating of three or higher leaves a video eligible
  Given an accepted video is rated three stars or higher
  When the public site is rebuilt
  Then the video remains eligible for public video indexes under the existing ordering rules

Scenario: filtering does not starve or distort paginated indexes
  Given an index has more videos than its configured lead, section, or page capacity, including videos rated two or lower before eligible videos in the source order
  When the public site is rebuilt and the index is paginated
  Then no video rated two or lower appears in any index slot or later page
  And eligible videos are reachable once without gaps or duplicates
  And low-rated videos do not consume slots or stop pagination
  And when fewer eligible videos remain than the configured capacity, the index stays shorter rather than filling with excluded videos

Scenario: direct editorial links are preserved
  Given an article or post contains a direct editorial link to a video rated two stars or lower
  When the public site is rebuilt
  Then that direct link remains available and resolves to the video

Scope: this rating exclusion applies only to video index listings. Do not change accepted status, direct article/post links, non-video content, or existing non-video listing policy. Unrated videos keep their current behavior.
